To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the deep-water sediment drift system on the New Zealand continental margin has a long history of development and evolution.

the evolution of the deep ocean circulation of the SW Pacific is recorded by the deposition of large Cenozoic sediment drifts on the New Zealand continental margin; the drifts were formed by the action of the DWBC and its precursor currents; the drifts are the most complete and detailed record of the evolution of deep ocean circulation in the Southern Ocean; the evolution of the DWCB is closely tied to the evolution of the ACC; and the deep ocean circulation system of the SW Pacific, and

the deep ocean circulation through the Southwest Pacific Gateway has been controlled by the interaction of the DWBC and the Antarctic Circumpolar Current since at least the Oligocene, with a history of increasing activity through the Cenozoic, and that the present-day DWBC is a product of the last 3 million years of this history.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the history of the DWBC and ACC, and of the deep-ocean circulation, from 25 to 5 Ma.
the evolution of the deep ocean circulation of the Southern Ocean, and of the deep western boundary current, since the early Cenozoic.
the history of the Pacific DWBC and related currents in the Southwest Pacific.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deep ocean circulation of the SW Pacific gateway is a complex system that has evolved through time.
the New Zealand margin provides the most complete and detailed record of deep-water circulation in the SW Pacific during the Neogene.

the evolution of the deep ocean circulation in the SW Pacific has been driven by the changing geometry of the New Zealand margin, which has controlled the delivery of sediment and water to the deep ocean.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DWBC and ACC are of late Cenozoic origin, and that their development was closely related to the evolution of the SW Pacific gateway.
the DWBC was active by the late Oligocene, and that the modern DWBC was in place by the late Miocene.
the New Zealand margin has been an ideal place to study the evolution of the ACC and DWBC systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deep ocean has always been a highly dynamic system, and that the modern deep ocean is the product of a very long and complex evolutionary history.
the modern DWBC is a relatively young phenomenon that commenced at ~5–6 Ma, and that it has been the major contributor of cold deep-water to the world ocean since that time.
the deep ocean circulation has been a key factor controlling the evolution of the Cenozoic climate system.
